genxml.title: Intel 82371AB PIIX4 (PCI-to-ISA bridge, IDE, USB, power management and SMBus) as wired in the Visual Workstation 320 and 540
genxml.doc: Register contract of the PIIX4 southbridge, functions 0 to 3, from the published datasheet and specification update, with the board wiring taken from the system firmware, the Windows NT hardware abstraction layer and the Linux Visual Workstation code. Grades: established means a datasheet or specification update page states it (the page is cited) or the shipped firmware and HAL do it in a routine read in full, which is a software expectation and not a measurement; inferred means a reasoned reading; unknown means no held source settles it. The update corrects the datasheet and wins where they differ. Config-space registers are in one space per PCI function (f0 ISA bridge, f1 IDE, f2 USB, f3 power management and SMBus). The power management block (pm), the SMBus block (smb), the IDE bus-master block (bm) and the fixed ISA ports (isa) are I/O spaces whose base is programmed in config space. Not listed: the 8259, 8254 and DMA controller registers (standard parts at their PC ports), the USB host controller I/O registers (no held software touches them at register level), and the device-monitor registers of function 3 (offsets 0x50 to 0x7f and the device activity and resource registers), which no held software writes.

struct.name: BM_CMD
struct.doc: Bus-master IDE command, primary channel; the secondary channel's is at +8 (bm_cmd_sec).

struct.name: BM_STATUS
struct.doc: Bus-master IDE status, primary channel; secondary channel's copy is at offset 0x0a.

struct.name: BM_PRD
struct.doc: Descriptor table pointer, primary channel; secondary channel's copy is at offset 0x0c.

struct.name: BM_CMD_SEC
struct.doc: Bus-master IDE command, secondary channel.

struct.name: BM_STATUS_SEC
struct.doc: Bus-master IDE status, secondary channel.

struct.name: BM_PRD_SEC
struct.doc: Descriptor table pointer, secondary channel.

struct.name: F0_VID
struct.doc: Vendor identification, Intel.

struct.name: F0_DID
struct.doc: Device identification of function 0. The firmware's self-test reads the function 0 vendor and device words as one dword and expects 0x71108086.

struct.name: F0_PCICMD
struct.doc: PCI command. The firmware writes 0x0f once. Bits 2 to 0 are hardwired to 1 and the bits the datasheet marks not implemented read 0, so the write leaves special cycle enable (bit 3) and SERR enable unchanged except bit 3 set; the special cycle enable is what lets the chip see the shutdown special cycle that Linux sends before powering off. The read-only mask lists the hardwired and reserved bits; only the fields shown are writable.

struct.name: F0_PCISTS
struct.doc: PCI status. Bits 14 to 11 are write-1-to-clear; DEVSEL# timing is medium (01).

struct.name: F0_RID
struct.doc: Revision. Stepping 00h initially; the specification update lists later values. Which stepping the board carries is not known.

struct.name: F0_CLASSC_PI
struct.doc: Class code, programming interface byte, 0x00. The PROM's register walk reads this dword once and discards the result.

struct.name: F0_CLASSC_SCC
struct.doc: Class code, sub-class byte: 0x01 (PCI-to-ISA bridge) while GENCFG bit 1 selects subtractive decode, 0x80 (other bridge) when it selects positive decode.

struct.name: F0_CLASSC_BASEC
struct.doc: Class code, base class byte, 0x06 (bridge).

struct.name: F0_HEDT
struct.doc: Header type, 0x80: a multifunction device. Functions 1 to 3 read their own header type as 0.

struct.name: F0_IORT
struct.doc: ISA I/O recovery timer. Reset enables 8-bit and 16-bit recovery with one SYSCLK added to the 3.5 SYSCLK minimum. Not written by any held software.

struct.name: F0_XBCS
struct.doc: X-bus chip select. The PROM writes the byte 0xf4: that sets the extended BIOS, lower BIOS, BIOSCS# write enable, coprocessor error and mouse functions and clears bits 1 and 0, the external keyboard and RTC chip selects (a software expectation). Clearing them while the Super I/O keyboard controller decodes its own ports is consistent with the board using the Super I/O's keyboard controller (inferred). Bit 9 and bit 7 forward the flash regions 0xfff00000 to 0xfff7ffff and 0xfff80000 to 0xfffdffff to the BIOS chip select; the top 64 KiB is always decoded. Which chip select the flash sits on is not stated by any source.

struct.name: F0_PIRQRC
struct.doc: PIRQ[A:D]# route control, one byte each at 0x60 to 0x63. The PROM writes 0x09 to the first (route PIRQA# to IRQ9). The routed IRQ must be level sensitive.

struct.name: F0_SERIRQC
struct.doc: Serial IRQ control. Not written by the PROM; GENCFG bit 16 must also select SERIRQ for it to take effect.

struct.name: F0_TOM
struct.doc: Top of memory and ISA/DMA forwarding. The PROM writes 0xf2: top of memory 16 MB and the 512-640 KB region forwarded to PCI.

struct.name: F0_MSTAT
struct.doc: Miscellaneous status.

struct.name: F0_MBDMA
struct.doc: Motherboard device DMA control, 0x76 and 0x77. The PROM writes 0x0c to both, which is the disabled channel (100) with the bit the datasheet says reads 1. The datasheet gives the default as 04h while saying bit 3 reads as 1; the two do not agree.

struct.name: F0_APICBASE
struct.doc: APIC base address relocation (the I/O APIC window follows the Intel 0xfec0 base). Not written by held software.

struct.name: F0_DLC
struct.doc: Deterministic latency control: delayed transaction, passive release and SERR# generation enables. Not written by held software.

struct.name: F0_PDMACFG
struct.doc: PCI DMA configuration: the DMA type of each channel. Channel 4 is the cascade and has no field. The PROM bit-walks the byte at 0x90 and the one at 0x95 (high byte of the channel 5 to 7 pointer) in its function 0 register test, and the walked bytes hold every pattern on the real board.

struct.name: F0_DDMABP
struct.doc: Distributed DMA slave base pointers: 0x92 for channels 0 to 3, 0x94 for channels 5 to 7; bits 15:6 are I/O address bits. The PROM bit-walks bytes 0x93 and 0x95 of these.

struct.name: F0_GENCFG
struct.doc: General configuration: pin function selects and bus mode. The PROM writes the bytes 0x4d (register 0xb0) and 0x60 (register 0xb3). 0x4d sets bit 0 (ISA mode, so the pins carry IOCHK# and LA[23:17] and are not GPI0 and GPO[7:1]), bit 6 (positive decode of the Plug and Play ports 0x279 and 0xa79) and the read-only bits 2 and 3, which stay as the straps set them. 0x60 sets bits 30 and 29, turning the RTCALE and RTCCS# pins into outputs GPO25 and GPO24. Bit 29 is printed as 'GPO2' in the datasheet and is GPO24 in its GPO table (a datasheet inconsistency). Tables 1 and 2 label the register 'PCI Function 1' but it is a function 0 register.

struct.name: F0_RTCCFG
struct.doc: Real-time clock configuration. The PROM writes 0x25 (positive decode, upper bank enable, RTC enable). The HAL sets bit 2 by read-modify-write before using the extended clock RAM at ports 0x72 and 0x73. The PROM's self-test clears and sets bit 0 around its clock RAM probe. The lock bits are write-once until a hardware reset. With bit 2 clear the datasheet says the access is forwarded to ISA (RTCCFG text) and also lists ports 0x72 to 0x77 as aliases of the index and data ports (Table 5); the two statements conflict.

struct.name: F1_VID
struct.doc: Vendor identification, Intel.

struct.name: F1_DID
struct.doc: Device identification of function 1.

struct.name: F1_PCICMD
struct.doc: PCI command. The PROM's IDE attach writes 5 (I/O space and bus master enable). The read-only mask lists the hardwired and reserved bits; only the fields shown are writable.

struct.name: F1_PCISTS
struct.doc: PCI status.

struct.name: F1_RID
struct.doc: Revision.

struct.name: F1_CLASSC_PI
struct.doc: Class code, programming interface (bus master capable, both channels legacy mode).

struct.name: F1_CLASSC_SCC
struct.doc: Class code, sub-class: IDE.

struct.name: F1_CLASSC_BASEC
struct.doc: Class code, base class: mass storage.

struct.name: F1_MLT
struct.doc: Master latency timer. The PROM's IDE attach writes 0x80.

struct.name: F1_HEDT
struct.doc: Header type, 0: single function (multifunction is reported by function 0).

struct.name: F1_BMIBA
struct.doc: Bus-master interface base address: I/O space, bits 15:4 are address bits, bit 0 hardwired 1.

struct.name: F1_IDETIM
struct.doc: IDE timing: 0x40 primary channel, 0x42 secondary. The PROM's IDE attach writes the dword 0xc077c077 (both channels: decode enabled, slave timing register enabled, fast timing with prefetch and IORDY sampling on both drives, ISP 5 clocks, RTC 4 clocks) and, on board type 1 (the 540, which has one IDE channel), writes the byte 0x40 to 0x43, which leaves only the slave timing enable set for the secondary channel and its decode disabled.

struct.name: F1_SIDETIM
struct.doc: Slave IDE timing (drive 1 of each channel) when IDETIM bit 14 is set. The PROM writes 0.

struct.name: F1_UDMACTL
struct.doc: Ultra DMA/33 enable per drive.

struct.name: F1_UDMATIM
struct.doc: Ultra DMA/33 cycle times, two bits per drive (00 CT 4 and RP 6 PCI clocks, 01 3 and 5, 10 2 and 4).

struct.name: F2_VID
struct.doc: Vendor identification, Intel.

struct.name: F2_DID
struct.doc: Device identification of function 2.

struct.name: F2_PCICMD
struct.doc: PCI command. The read-only mask lists the hardwired and reserved bits; only the fields shown are writable.

struct.name: F2_PCISTS
struct.doc: PCI status.

struct.name: F2_RID
struct.doc: Revision.

struct.name: F2_CLASSC_PI
struct.doc: Class code, programming interface: OpenHCI-style USB host controller.

struct.name: F2_CLASSC_SCC
struct.doc: Class code, sub-class: USB.

struct.name: F2_CLASSC_BASEC
struct.doc: Class code, base class: serial bus.

struct.name: F2_MLT
struct.doc: Master latency timer.

struct.name: F2_HEDT
struct.doc: Header type, 0.

struct.name: F2_USBBA
struct.doc: USB I/O space base address: bits 15:5, bit 0 hardwired 1. The datasheet's default of 00h disagrees with bit 0 being hardwired to 1; the reset here is 1 (inferred).

struct.name: F2_INTLN
struct.doc: Interrupt line; no effect on the hardware.

struct.name: F2_INTPN
struct.doc: Interrupt pin, hardwired 4 (INTD#). The datasheet says the USB interrupt is also ORed to PIRQD#; the board wires only this pin to its own interrupt entry, never through the 8259.

struct.name: F2_SBRNUM
struct.doc: Serial bus release number, 0x10 (USB 1.0).

struct.name: F2_LEGSUP
struct.doc: Legacy keyboard and mouse support: trap and SMI enables and status. Not written by held software.

struct.name: F2_MISCSUP
struct.doc: Miscellaneous support: bit 4 lets a read of port 0x70 return the RTC index. Byte accesses only.

struct.name: F3_VID
struct.doc: Vendor identification, Intel.

struct.name: F3_DID
struct.doc: Device identification of function 3.

struct.name: F3_PCICMD
struct.doc: PCI command. Bit 0 enables the SMBus I/O block and works independently of PMREGMISC bit 0. The PROM's function 3 attach sets it after writing the SMBus base. The read-only mask lists the hardwired and reserved bits; only the fields shown are writable.

struct.name: F3_PCISTS
struct.doc: PCI status; the PROM's attach clears it by writing 0x3800.

struct.name: F3_RID
struct.doc: Revision.

struct.name: F3_CLASSC_PI
struct.doc: Class code, programming interface.

struct.name: F3_CLASSC_SCC
struct.doc: Class code, sub-class: other bridge.

struct.name: F3_CLASSC_BASEC
struct.doc: Class code, base class: bridge.

struct.name: F3_HEDT
struct.doc: Header type, 0.

struct.name: F3_INTLN
struct.doc: Interrupt line. The datasheet (p.120) says it has no effect on the hardware. Specification update spec change 9 (p.15) says the register 'is not implemented and is RESERVED'.

struct.name: F3_INTPN
struct.doc: Interrupt pin: not implemented. The datasheet (p.120) says it is read only, default 01h, and that PIRQA# is used for the power management module. Specification update spec change 1 (p.13) retitles it 'INTPN Register Not Implemented' and says: 'the INTPN register indicates the PCI interrupt pin PIRQA# is used for routing Serial Interrupts. However, Serial Interrupts are hardwired to IRQ9. This register is not implemented.' It lists bits 7:0 as Not Implemented with default 00h. The datasheet's pin A is superseded. The update says 'Serial Interrupts'; that this means the power management and SMBus interrupts is our reading (inferred). What a read returns is taken as 0 from the update's default.

struct.name: F3_PMBA
struct.doc: Power management base address. Bits 15:6 hold the I/O base, bit 0 is hardwired 1, bits 31:16 are hardwired 0. The PROM writes 0x0f80 and the register then reads 0x0f81; the base 0xf80 is what Linux and the HAL assume. The HAL never programs it.

struct.name: F3_CNTA
struct.doc: Idle timer counts and resolutions for the device monitors and the slow burst count. Not written by held software.

struct.name: F3_CNTB
struct.doc: Fast burst timer count, CPU select, thermal duty and video status. The specification update (spec change 5) corrects bit 5 to 8 microsecond granularity. Not written by held software.

struct.name: F3_GPICTL
struct.doc: General purpose input control: enable, polarity and edge for the device-monitor GPI inputs (Table 17 maps GPI18 to GPI21 to device monitors 10 to 13). Not written by held software.

struct.name: F3_PMREGMISC
struct.doc: Miscellaneous power management. The PROM writes 1 after the base. When the bit is clear every access to the power management block goes unclaimed.

struct.name: F3_SMBBA
struct.doc: SMBus base address: bits 15:4, bit 0 hardwired 1. The PROM's function 3 attach writes 0x0fd0, so the register reads 0x00000fd1 (not read back by any held software); neither HAL build touches it.

struct.name: F3_SMBHSTCFG
struct.doc: SMBus host configuration. The PROM writes 0x09: host interface enabled and the interrupt routed to IRQ9.

struct.name: F3_SMBSLVC
struct.doc: SMBus slave command match value.

struct.name: F3_SMBSHDW1
struct.doc: SMBus slave shadow port 1.

struct.name: F3_SMBSHDW2
struct.doc: SMBus slave shadow port 2.

struct.name: F3_SMBREV
struct.doc: SMBus revision.

struct.name: RIRQ
struct.doc: Reset X-bus IRQ12/M and IRQ1: a read clears the latched mouse and keyboard interrupts; the read value has no defined pattern. Reads and writes are also sent to ISA.

struct.name: NMISC
struct.doc: NMI status and control. Bits 7:4 are read-only status (SERR# NMI source, IOCHK# NMI source, counter 2 output, refresh toggle) and must be written as 0.

struct.name: RTCI
struct.doc: RTC index and NMI enable, shared. Bits 6:0 index the lower RTC bank and are undefined at reset (the datasheet gives only 'Bit[6:0]=undefined; Bit 7=1', p.84); bit 7 set disables NMI. Write only. The PROM and the HAL reach the clock through ports 0x70 and 0x71.

struct.name: RTCD
struct.doc: RTC data, lower 128-byte bank.

struct.name: RTCEI
struct.doc: RTC extended index: bits 6:0 address the upper bank (the datasheet lists it write only in its register page and read/write in Table 5). Bit 7 is the aliased NMI enable according to specification update spec change 2 (p.13); the datasheet calls it reserved. The upper bank is reached only with RTCCFG bit 2 set.

struct.name: RTCED
struct.doc: RTC extended data, upper 128-byte bank (battery-backed RAM).

struct.name: P92
struct.doc: Port 92. The PROM never writes it; the application processors set bit 1. The datasheet text says FAST_A20 set asserts A20M# low but its own table and specification update documentation change 11 (p.54) say a 1 deasserts A20M#.

struct.name: APMC
struct.doc: APM control port; a write can raise an SMI#.

struct.name: APMS
struct.doc: APM status port.

struct.name: CERR
struct.doc: Coprocessor error: a write asserts IGNNE# if FERR# is asserted and negates internal IRQ13; any value. Reads and writes flow through to ISA.

struct.name: RC
struct.doc: Reset control. Linux restarts the board by writing 0x06 (reset CPU with system reset set); the HAL does the same on all but the earliest boards. Bit 2 going 0 to 1 starts the reset; bit 1 chooses a hard reset (1) or a soft INIT-only reset (0).

struct.name: PMSTS
struct.doc: Power management status. The HAL clears it and reads bit 8 for the power button; the PROM reads it for wake-up state and writes it back to clear.

struct.name: PMEN
struct.doc: Power management resume enable. The PROM and the HAL write 0x0100 (power button).

struct.name: PMCNTRL
struct.doc: Power management control. Linux powers off, and the HAL suspends, by writing 0x2000 (suspend enable with type 0, soft off). The PROM writes 0x1401 (working type, SCI enabled) at attach and 0x2000 to power down.

struct.name: PMTMR
struct.doc: Power management timer: a free-running 24-bit counter at 3.579545 MHz; bit 23 toggling sets TMROF_STS. The register summary table (p.51) lists the register as R/W while its description (p.139) says read only; this unit takes read only.

struct.name: GPSTS
struct.doc: General purpose status. The PROM reads it (0xf8c) for wake-up and power-fail state.

struct.name: GPEN
struct.doc: General purpose enable. The PROM's function 3 attach writes 0 (0xf8e).

struct.name: PCNTRL
struct.doc: Processor control: throttling, clock control and PCI clock run enables. Not written by held software.

struct.name: PLVL2
struct.doc: Processor level 2: a read enters stop grant or quick start.

struct.name: PLVL3
struct.doc: Processor level 3: a read enters stop clock, sleep or deep sleep.

struct.name: GLBSTS
struct.doc: Global status. Bits 10, 8, 5, 2, 1 and 0 are write-1-to-clear; bits 7, 6 and 4 are read only summaries. Bit 11 is labelled R/W in the datasheet but also 'can only be reset by writing a 1', so it is not in the write-1-to-clear mask here (p.143).

struct.name: DEVSTS
struct.doc: Device status: idle and trap status of the device monitors.

struct.name: GLBEN
struct.doc: Global enable.

struct.name: GLBCTL
struct.doc: Global control: SMI enable, end of SMI, BIOS release, global standby timer.

struct.name: DEVCTL
struct.doc: Device control: trap and idle enables of the device monitors.

struct.name: GPIREG
struct.doc: General purpose input, byte reads only (offsets 0x30 to 0x32; the byte at 0x33 is not listed). Bits 21:0 are the logical value on pins GPI21 to GPI0; GPI13 to GPI21 and GPI1 are not multiplexed, the others need their select bit. A bit that is not configured as an input reads indeterminate. The register is not reset; it follows the pins. Port 0xfb2 is byte 2.

struct.name: GPOREG
struct.from: Intel 82371AB datasheet 290562-001 (April 1997) p.148; Intel 82371AB specification update 297738-017 (January 2002) p.23
struct.doc: General purpose output, byte accesses only (ports 0xfb4 to 0xfb7). Bits 30:0 drive GPO30 to GPO0 and read back the last value written; a pin shared with another function follows that function until GENCFG or XBCS selects the output. The reset value 0x7fffbfff is the datasheet's default (p.148) and the specification update's erratum 3 (p.23) gives the actual value per bit: bit 31 has no output, bits 30:15 and 13:0 reset to 1 and bit 14 to 0. Port 0xfb5 therefore resets to 0xbf.

struct.name: SMBHSTSTS
struct.doc: SMBus host status: failed, bus collision, device error, interrupt (all write 1 to clear) and host busy. The PROM clears it by writing before its one transaction.

struct.name: SMBSLVSTS
struct.doc: SMBus slave status.

struct.name: SMBHSTCNT
struct.doc: SMBus host control. The PROM's single transaction writes 0x54 (start, block protocol); reading the register resets the block data index.

struct.name: SMBHSTCMD
struct.doc: SMBus host command field.

struct.name: SMBHSTADD
struct.doc: SMBus host address: bits 7:1 slave address, bit 0 read (1) or write (0).

struct.name: SMBHSTDAT0
struct.doc: SMBus host data 0 (byte count for block transfers).

struct.name: SMBHSTDAT1
struct.doc: SMBus host data 1.

struct.name: SMBBLKDAT
struct.doc: SMBus block data port.

struct.name: SMBSLVCNT
struct.doc: SMBus slave control.

struct.name: SMBSHDWCMD
struct.doc: SMBus shadow command: command received by an external master access to the slave or shadow ports.

struct.name: SMBSLVEVT
struct.doc: SMBus slave event: data bits compared with incoming slave data.

struct.name: SMBSLVDAT
struct.doc: SMBus slave data: data received by an external master access to the slave or shadow ports.
